title: U.S. House · Ohio's 1st District
area: Includes most of Cincinnati and Hamilton County

context.text: Ohio redrew its congressional map ahead of 2026 under a new Ohio Redistricting Commission plan. The Cook Political Report rates the 1st District R+1.

summary.text: Greg Landsman is the Democratic incumbent for Ohio's 1st District, a Cincinnati native who worked in education nonprofits and state government, led a Cincinnati preschool ballot measure, and served on the Cincinnati City Council before his 2022 election to Congress. He serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee and is seeking a third term.

background.text: Born in Cincinnati in 1976 and lives in Mt. Washington, Ohio.
Earned a B.A. in economics and political science from Ohio University (1999) and an M.A. in theological studies, religion, and public policy from Harvard University (2004).
Describes himself as a former teacher and the son of teachers who spent most of his career working on behalf of children and families.
Worked as executive director of The Strive Partnership with the KnowledgeWorks Foundation and as director of the Ohio Governor's Office of Faith-Based and Community Initiatives.
Led a ballot measure to make Cincinnati the first city in America to provide two years of preschool, according to his congressional biography.

Served on the Cincinnati City Council from 2018 to 2022; his congressional biography cites work on eviction prevention reforms and investments in prenatal care, child care, affordable housing and youth jobs.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2022, succeeding Steve Chabot, and took office in January 2023.

Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, including its Health, Communications and Technology, and Environment subcommittees. Co-chairs the bipartisan What Works Caucus and co-founded the Lowering Costs Caucus, according to his congressional biography.
Lives in Cincinnati with his wife, Sarah, and their two children, according to his congressional biography.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Environment; Health; Communications and Technology subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Said on July 19, 2024 that President Joe Biden should withdraw from the 2024 Democratic presidential race, saying 'It is time for President Biden to step aside and allow us to nominate a new leader who can reliably and consistently make the case against Donald Trump and make the case for the future of America.'

summary.text: Eric Conroy is the Republican nominee, a Cincinnati native, U.S. Air Force Academy graduate and Air Force veteran who later worked as a CIA case officer. He announced his candidacy in July 2025 and says he is running on national security, border security, fiscal responsibility and energy independence.

background.text: Born and raised on the West Side of Cincinnati; graduated from Elder High School.
Graduated from the U.S. Air Force Academy in 2011 and served in the U.S. Air Force from 2011 to 2018.
Later worked overseas in national security as a CIA case officer, according to his campaign materials; Fox News described him as a former CIA case officer when he announced his campaign.
Earned a graduate degree from Columbia University in 2025.
Announced his campaign for Ohio's 1st District in July 2025 and has been endorsed by U.S. Sen. Bernie Moreno, according to his Ballotpedia survey.

priorities.text: Says national security and border security must be restored, supporting 'strong border enforcement, modernizing our immigration system, and ensuring that federal law is consistently upheld.'
priorities.quote: National security and border security must be restored. A safe nation is the foundation for prosperity.

priorities.text: Calls for fiscal responsibility, citing federal spending as a driver of inflation, and says he will 'advocate for responsible budgeting, reducing waste, and policies that promote economic growth and job creation.'
Supports energy independence and expanding domestic energy production and American manufacturing.

positions.summary: Supports stronger border enforcement and says federal immigration law should be consistently upheld.
positions.quote: I support strong border enforcement, modernizing our immigration system, and ensuring that federal law is consistently upheld to protect American communities and sovereignty.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he will 'stand with law enforcement, oppose defunding the police.'
positions.quote: Eric Conroy will stand with law enforcement, oppose defunding the police, and fight for policies that keep violent criminals off our streets.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he will 'be a steadfast ally of Israel and our national security.'
positions.quote: Eric Conroy will strengthen America's military, invest in next-generation defense, and be a steadfast ally of Israel and our national security.

summary.text: Nathan Weise is the Libertarian Party nominee, a software engineer and University of Cincinnati graduate who has held roles in the Ohio and Hamilton County Libertarian parties. He describes his campaign as focused on affordability, ending foreign wars and immigration reform.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Cincinnati in 2013, where he says his interest in politics began.
Joined the Libertarian Party in 2012; says he later earned a Master of Public Administration degree. Ballotpedia lists a graduate degree from Grand Canyon University (2019).

Has served as communications director for the Ohio Libertarian Party, represented Ohio at the Libertarian National Convention, and chairs the Hamilton County Libertarian Party, according to his Ballotpedia survey.

priorities.text: Supports 'responsible spending reforms' to address inflation and make homeownership more attainable, under the message 'Make America Affordable Again.'
Supports ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars and reducing the number of U.S. military bases abroad.
Supports an 'Ellis Island-style' immigration policy that eases entry and provides a path to permanent residency, and opposes militarized border enforcement.

positions.summary: Supports easier legal immigration and opposes militarized immigration enforcement; says he would abolish ICE.
positions.quote: He supports eliminating the militarization of border security and immigration enforcement, believing that force should not be used against individuals who are not violent. Abolish ICE and replace it with nothing.
